correctness.rationale: The upset normal form partitions H by the first occupied antichain level. The relative-pseudocomplement formula yields an if-and-only-if higher-witness condition for equality of Peirce consequent and antecedent. Applying it to partial levels and full tails identifies the fibers as principal filters of exact sizes. A disjoint multiplicity count proves the generating polynomial for every positive width, including h=1; strictly increasing exponents imply unique recovery of all ordered widths. Summing the fiber sizes gives the exact scalar failure formula. Included verify.py independently checked all 255 ordered width compositions of sizes at most eight and five larger tuples, 328293 ordered Peirce pairs, exact fiber sets, coefficients, inverse reconstruction, and direct residuation in 31 small cases. The unrestricted theorem follows from the proof, not finite enumeration.

originality.rationale: The principal primary paper gives general Peirce law as a classical principle and proves that its degree of satisfiability has no finite gap, without the conditional right-fiber rank polynomial or inverse reconstruction for stacked antichains. Direct mathematical-literature queries and mathematically adjacent prior statements did not reveal a result implying the simultaneous exact fiber classification and isomorphism invariant. The implication comparison excludes the established no-gap result and standard upset semantics from the novelty claim. Equivalent uncatalogued work remains possible; novelty is assessed, not externally certified.

value.rationale: The multiset of conditional satisfiability fibers is an intrinsic logical-statistical invariant. For all finite weak-order Heyting algebras, it recovers the entire ordered level-size sequence and hence the frame and algebra isomorphism types, a qualitatively stronger classification than a mean probability. The pair (2,3) versus (3,2) proves why the scalar mean loses essential order information and why the more precise invariant is mathematically motivated. The result is an all-parameter classification, not a routine recalculation of the known finite Peirce no-gap statement.
